units: Ab. Zar. 65ᵃ הרי הוא כמ׳ שבאומות he is legally treated like an infidel of the gentiles, i.e. like a gentile that has rejected the gods of his people.—Esp. Min, a Jewish infidel, mostly applied to Jew-Christians (and in editions controlled by censors, often substituted by צדוקי, כותי &c.).

<cite ref="Horayot 11a:17">Hor. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>להכעיס הרי זה מ׳</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>צדוקי</he>) if he eats forbidden fat in a defiant manner (v. <cite ref="K00970"><he>כָּעַס</he></cite>), he is a Min; <cite ref="Horayot 11a:19">ib.</cite> (another opin.) <he>איזהו מ׳ כל העובד ע״ז</he> who is a Min? (A Jew) who worships idols.—

<cite ref="Gittin 45b:10">Gitt. 45ᵇ</cite> <he>ס״ת שכתבו מ׳</he> a book of the Law written by a Min, contrad. to <cite ref="N00847"><he>נכרי</he></cite>; a. fr.—Pl. <he>מִינִים</he>, <he>מִינִין</he>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:1:8">Y. Ber. IX, 12ᵈ</cite> bot. <he>המ׳ שאלו את וכ׳</he> the Minin asked R. Simlai &c.

<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Metzia 2:33">Tosef. B. Mets. II, 33</cite> <he>המ׳ והמשומדים והמסורות</he> the Minin, the apostates and the informers; <cite ref="Avodah Zarah 26b:4">Ab. Zar. 26ᵇ</cite> (Rashi: idolatrous priests, Jews or gentiles); a. fr.—<he>בִּרְכַת הַמִּ׳</he> the (twelfth) section inserted in the Prayer of Benedictions and containing an imprecation against the Minim.
